plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single labeled diagram of an upward-opening parabola drawn on a Cartesian coordinate plane, with thin black arrowed axes crossing near the lower left of the curve and marked x at the right and y at the top. The parabola is a heavy dark blue curve whose two branches end in arrowheads pointing up and outward. Its lowest point is a filled dark blue dot above the horizontal x-axis, connected by a short leader line to the label Vertex at the left. A dashed orange vertical line rises through that dot and carries the orange label Axis of symmetry at the upper right. Directly above the vertex on that same vertical line sits a small teal dot labeled Focus in teal. A short dashed blue horizontal segment runs through the teal dot from one branch of the curve to the other and is tagged Latus rectum by a curved arrow from the upper left. Below the vertex, a dashed red horizontal line spanning the width of the frame is labeled Directrix in red, and the x-axis lies lower in the frame. Color-coding the four named features separately lets the reader see that the axis of symmetry meets the directrix at a right angle and that the vertex lies midway between focus and directrix. The drawing establishes the vocabulary used to define a parabola as the set of points equally distant from the focus and the directrix.

interactionPlan.concept: A parabola is the set of points equidistant from a fixed point (focus) and a fixed line (directrix), and the parameter p — the distance from vertex to focus — controls both the curve's width and the positions of all its named features.
elements: x-axis with arrowhead at right, labeled x
y-axis with arrowhead at top, labeled y
upward-opening parabola curve in dark blue with arrowheads on both branches
vertex: filled dark blue dot at the parabola's lowest point, labeled 'Vertex'
axis of symmetry: dashed orange vertical line through the vertex, labeled 'Axis of symmetry'
focus: small teal filled dot on the axis of symmetry above the vertex, labeled 'Focus'
latus rectum: dashed blue horizontal segment through the focus spanning between the two branches, labeled 'Latus rectum'
directrix: dashed red horizontal line below the vertex spanning the frame width, labeled 'Directrix'
sample point on the parabola (for distance construction mode)
perpendicular segment from sample point to focus (for distance construction mode)
perpendicular segment from sample point to directrix (for distance construction mode)
equal-length tick marks or labels on both distance segments

interactions.label: Focus–directrix distance p
interactions.teaches: The single parameter p simultaneously sets the focus height, directrix depth, latus rectum width, and parabola curvature — one number controls the entire shape

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching to the distance construction reveals that every point on the parabola is exactly as far from the focus as from the directrix — this equal-distance property is the definition, not a consequence
Each named feature (vertex, focus, directrix, axis of symmetry, latus rectum) has a precise geometric role; hovering isolates one at a time so the vocabulary builds without visual clutter

demo_steps.title: Meet the parts
demo_steps.narration: The parabola's anatomy: vertex at the turning point, focus above it, directrix below it, axis of symmetry through both, and latus rectum spanning the curve at the focus's height. Hover each feature to see its role.

demo_steps.title: One number shapes everything
demo_steps.narration: Drag p larger: the focus rises, the directrix drops, the latus rectum widens, and the parabola flattens. Drag p smaller and everything compresses. A single distance parameter controls the entire figure.

demo_steps.title: The equal-distance definition
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the distance construction: a sample point on the curve connects to the focus and drops perpendicularly to the directrix — both segments are always equal in length. This is not a property of parabolas; it IS the definition.

demo_steps.title: Definition holds for any p
demo_steps.narration: Now drag p while in distance-construction mode: the equal-length segments stretch or shrink together, confirming the definition holds regardless of the parabola's width.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The parabola is not defined by its equation — it is defined by the equal-distance condition to a point and a line, and the parameter p is the single number that scales every feature simultaneously.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Cartesian axes in thin black with arrowheads; parabola in heavy dark blue (#1a3a5c or similar) with arrowheads on both upper branches. Vertex as a filled dark blue circle. Axis of symmetry as a dashed orange vertical line. Focus as a small teal (#2ab5a0) filled circle. Latus rectum as a dashed medium-blue horizontal segment. Directrix as a dashed red horizontal line. In distance-construction mode, draw a draggable sample point on the parabola with two colored segments (e.g., green to focus, purple to directrix) marked with equal-length ticks. Labels in their respective colors matching the feature they name. The vertex should sit at approximately (1, 1) in the default view so all features are visible within the frame. When p changes, the vertex stays fixed and focus/directrix move symmetrically about it.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for changing the focus-directrix distance p: the learner drags p, the focus rises or falls with the directrix mirroring below the vertex and the blue parabola widens or narrows, making the equal-distance definition control the curve's shape.
- Toggle between labeled features and distance construction: the learner switches views, labels fade into perpendicular distance segments from a sample point to the focus and directrix, making clear why the vertex sits midway between them.
- Hover for individual parabola features: the learner hovers the vertex, focus, directrix, axis, or latus rectum, the selected feature brightens with its label and related construction lines, clarifying each vocabulary term without crowding the diagram.

authoredContext:
In Quadratic Functions, we learned about a parabola’s vertex and axis of symmetry. Now we extend the discussion to include other key features of the parabola. See the figure. Notice that the axis of symmetry passes through the focus and vertex and is perpendicular to the directrix. The vertex is the midpoint between the directrix and the focus.

The line segment that passes through the focus and is parallel to the directrix is called the latus rectum. The endpoints of the latus rectum lie on the curve. By definition, the distance d from the focus to any point P on the parabola is equal to the distance from P to the directrix.

Key features of the parabola

This image displays a parabola on a Cartesian coordinate plane, clearly labeling its fundamental geometric elements. The blue curve represents the parabola itself. The "Vertex" is indicated as the turning point of the parabola. Inside the curve, the "Focus" is marked, a critical point for defining the parabola. A dashed orange line, labeled "Axis of symmetry", passes vertically through both the vertex and the focus. Below the vertex, a horizontal dashed red line shows the "Directrix". Finally, a horizontal dashed blue line segment passing through the focus and extending to the parabola is identified as the "Latus rectum".

To work with parabolas in the coordinate plane, we consider two cases: those with a vertex at the origin and those with a vertex at a point other than the origin. We begin with the former.

discrepancies: The focus is drawn as a filled circle, whereas the source uses a distinctive teal diamond marker.
The red directrix coincides exactly with the x-axis (y=0) in the generated figure, while the source shows a clear vertical gap between the directrix and the x-axis.
The 'Latus rectum' label in the source has a leader arrow pointing to the dashed blue chord; the generated version places bare text with no pointer.
The parabola stroke is a darker navy (#1a3a5c) than the medium blue used in the source figure.
evaluation.notes: All five anatomical features (vertex, focus, directrix, axis of symmetry, latus rectum) are present with correct colors, correct chord endpoints (length 4p), and a strong interaction set (p-slider, equal-distance construction toggle with draggable point, 4-step player); main weaknesses are the focus drawn as a circle instead of a diamond, the directrix sitting on the x-axis rather than above it, and a missing leader arrow on the latus-rectum label.
action_items: Render the focus as a teal diamond (rotated square) to match the source marker instead of a circle.
Adjust the default vertex/parameter (e.g. k=1.5 with p=1) or shift the x-axis down so the directrix has a visible gap above the x-axis as in the source.
Add a short leader arrow from the 'Latus rectum' text to the dashed blue chord.
Move the draw.on('mousemove')/on('mouseup') drag handlers out of drawDistance() so they are attached once, preventing listener accumulation on every redraw.

feedback.rationale: Overall average of 4.2 with no failure modes, concept accuracy of 5, and only minor cosmetic discrepancies (marker shape, leader arrow, slight positioning) — further iteration is unlikely to yield meaningful improvement.
